name: shibumi-beach-caddy
description: Phase 2 of the Shibumi-adapters program: ONE combined caddy that mounts to the Shibumi beach chair (via the Phase-1 capture socket) and holds a phone, a Kindle, and a Yeti bottle together, ergonomically. Prefer UNIBODY (single print, capture socket integrated). Parameterized PER PERSON so a second owner's caddy (Hana) is a dimension swap, not a redesign. v0 = architecture/massing stage: packaging + structural reasoning locked, geometry pending open decisions (Yeti diameter, chair load path, final layout).
requiresId_note: Utility part; 'ergonomic' handled as functional layout, not aesthetic motif. Revisit if Matt wants styling.
material_note: PLA for fit/massing prototypes. Final beach part PETG or ASA (UV + hot-trunk + load). Geometry kept material-agnostic.

program.mount_interface: socket backing face, 28.2 x 40.1 mm, r3.0, in the -Z plane; gap-independent so caddy design is NOT blocked by the pending A/B/C fit-test
program.recommended_coupling: UNIBODY — integrate the capture socket into the caddy; no separable joint. See ARCHITECTURE.md for why (removes the weakest link under a full-bottle moment).

phone.note: iPhone IN CASE. Caliper maxed on H -> ~156 is a FLOOR, likely slightly more. t=15 includes camera bump.

kindle.note: Caliper maxed on H -> ~176 is a FLOOR.

bottle.note: CONFIRMED by Matt (WM#592, 2026-07-25): the 96mm is the DIAMETER (~36oz-class Yeti). Bottle oz still assumed ~36 for mass estimate.

hana.note: Hana gets her OWN caddy with her devices' dims. Design stays parameterized so this is a re-slice, not a re-model.

design_margins.note: Applied to a person's raw dims to get modeled interior envelopes.
design_margins.tall_dim_hold_fraction: cradle holds a lower portion; item protrudes for grab. Add extra height margin since tall dims are caliper-maxed floors.

loadCase.note: PRELIMINARY — refine once geometry + chair load path are known. Governs requiresStrainAnalysis=true.
loadCase.bottle_mass_note: bottle ~0.45kg + up to ~1L water; use 1.2-1.5kg. Confirm bottle size (26/36/46oz) with Matt.
loadCase.lever_arm_concern: all mass cantilevers off a ~28x40mm cleat socket. Overturning moment ~1.5-2 N*m estimated.
loadCase.design_directive: STANDALONE CANTILEVER (WM#1104, Matt, 2026-07-28): the caddy must NOT rely on backing against the chair leg — the cleat protrudes awkwardly (forces the caddy back + leaning) and the leg fit is a hard-to-capture 3D skew. The cleat-mount + gussets carry the FULL cantilever load rigidly. An OPTIONAL leg brace can be added later IF Matt supplies the leg-skew dims; it is a bonus, not load-bearing.
loadCase.v3_mitigations: (1) heavy bottle nearest the mount + low = shortest lever arm; (2) external SIDE BUTTRESS GUSSETS run the full depth along the load path, deepest at the root; (3) BACK-CORNER HAUNCHES fillet the base<->spine junction where the moment peaks; (4) thicker base plate (5.5) + spine (8.0) = deeper root section; (5) unibody, no coupling to peel; (6) PRINT BASE-DOWN so the peak tensile fiber runs in-plane with the layers, junction loaded in shear/compression not interlayer peel.
loadCase.next: strain-analyzer pass on this geometry to quantify root stress + safety factor and confirm the section is adequate standalone; escalate to FEA if the margin is tight (gusseted junction is not a clean prism).
loadCase.material_note: PETG primary (final part PETG or ASA per material_note top-level; ASA not in scad-lib/materials.json yet so PETG used as the closest analyzed proxy — similar ductility/interlayer behavior). See strain-analyzer discussion for a PLA one-liner (fit prototypes print PLA).

forces.comment: Full Yeti bottle (~1.5kg incl. water) resting in the cradle; y=bo_cy (cradle centerline), z arbitrary mid-cradle-height (gravity moment about the X bending axis depends only on the Y offset for this geometry, not Z).
Kindle in its channel (0.2kg), y = mid-channel centroid (y_k0..y_k1 midpoint).
iPhone in case, in its channel (0.25kg), y = mid-channel centroid (y_p0..y_p1 midpoint).

Caddy self-weight (0.5kg est., base+spine+gussets+haunches+cradle wall). Y-centroid ~50mm from the root, volume-weighted across spine (heavy, at the very back), gussets (triangular, centroid at 1/3 of their 170mm run), base plate (uniform across full depth), and bottle-cradle wall — cross-checked against the spec narrative estimate of ~1.5-2 N*m total overturning moment (this force set sums to ~1.83 N*m at the root, consistent).

criticalSections.name: root-spine-mount-junction
criticalSections.comment: Full-width solid spine block (caddy_w x spine_h) at y=0, the base<->spine/mount junction named in the design brief as the peak-moment section. Printed base-down per the v3 directive, so the peak tensile/compressive fiber (top/bottom of this section) runs fore-aft (Y) = in-plane with the horizontal layers, not interlayer peel. This model captures ONLY the solid spine block; it deliberately ignores the two side buttress gussets and the back-corner haunches (extra, unquantified reinforcement) that also cross this junction, so it is a conservative FLOOR on the true section strength, not the true composite. Not a clean prism once gussets/haunches are counted -> FEA recommended for an exact composite number, though the margin here should be enormous given the base_t/spine_t upsizing.

criticalSections.name: gusset-taper-post-spine
criticalSections.comment: Idealizes the TWO side buttress gussets alone (each 4.5mm thick x taper height, combined as one 9mm-wide equivalent rect since gusset X-position does not affect bending resistance about the X axis) at y=9mm, just aft of the spine, where the spine's full 140x110 block ends and the tapering gusset+base-plate composite becomes the sole flexural member for the rest of the cantilever (y=9..170). Height 70.5mm = linear taper value at y=9 (gusset_h=74mm at y=0 -> 0 at y=170, per side_gusset() polygon). Deliberately ignores the 5.5mm base plate and haunch fillets underneath (extra, unquantified reinforcement) -> conservative FLOOR. Gussets print as vertical ribs, base-down, so bending stress (fore-aft) runs in-plane with horizontal layers, not interlayer peel. Not a clean prism (two separate outboard ribs, not a solid block) -> FEA recommended for an exact composite number. Hand-swept check across y=9..160 (not run through this single-point CLI section) shows stress stays under ~0.22 MPa throughout this region -- well below either candidate section here -- so no additional mid-span section is expected to govern.

open_items: MOUNT/LOAD-PATH ONLY (does NOT block the body): chair geometry around the cleat (photos) + whether the caddy can rest against the chair frame. Determines if a single cleat mount is structurally sufficient.
MOUNT ONLY: Phase-1 A/B/C fit-test result -> sets the integrated capture socket's rail_height. Socket is modeled as a parametric TBD placeholder until then.
Bottle oz refinement (assumed ~36oz for mass; confirm).
